_min_tradable_equity_usd_note: Operator override of the derived floor. The derived value is what every enabled book needs to hold a position AT ONCE; below it the first book to fire consumes the budget and the rest sit margin-blocked, which looks from outside like books that do not fire (W-FUND1). $26.0 also acts as a drawdown brake: the system stops rather than grinding down.
_sizing_note:
2026-09-07: DE-RISKED TO VALIDATE. Deployment cut 98% -> 40.4% because the operator is capital-constrained and the book is UNVALIDATED (live forward record 0/6; backtest +1.408% n=2562 has not been confirmed forward).
THE KEY FACT THAT MAKES THIS FREE: evidence accrues at the SAME RATE at any deployment. xs_reversal_live.py:268 records every candidate to the shadow ledger BEFORE any position, claim or execute logic - the gates above it are data gates (no universe, no panel, universe too small, no candidates), never capital gates. So cutting size costs zero learning. Being 98% deployed on 6 resolved bets was maximum risk against minimum evidence.
NOT shadow_only, deliberately: line 213 returns BEFORE the ledger write, so shadow_only records NOTHING and would stop the validation entirely. Small live size also keeps real fills, real slippage and real funding in the record, which a paper run cannot produce.
SIZED FROM THE EXCHANGE MINIMUM UP, not from equity down: frac = 10.5/(26 x 3) = 0.13462, the smallest fraction whose position still clears HL's $10.5 minimum AT THE $26 FLOOR. Any smaller and orders start being refused exactly as the account shrinks.
  one position stops   6.1% of equity
  daily kill           12.1%  (between one stop-out and a full one)
  all 3 stop together  18.2%  -- was 44.1%
TO SCALE BACK UP once the ledger has ~37 resolved bets: raise strategy_book_equity_frac and min_available_margin_pct together, and let tests/test_live_config_coherence.py tell you what else must move.
_xyz_concentration_note:
max_xyz_short_names 3 = max_concurrent, so the name cap never refuses a slot the concurrency budget already approved. It used to sit at 2 with max_concurrent 2 and produced 'REFUSED SHORT xyz:SNDK - xyz-short name cap reached (2/2)' while slots were free.
max_xyz_short_notional_pct 2.815 is the deployment expressed as notional: 92% of equity as margin x 3x = 2.76x equity, plus 2% slack. It is a PERCENT and has to be - it scales with the account, where a dollar cap would go stale in both directions.
Why it is not smaller: xyz shorts are ~1.28 effective bets at 0.83 mean pairwise correlation (W-MATH2/3; seven stopped together on 07-21 for -$8.59). The gate measures NOTIONAL and is right to - a correlated 15% move costs 15% of notional whatever the leverage. Sizing the book therefore means accepting a 41.4% correlated drawdown, which is why that number is declared explicitly in max_correlated_drawdown_pct rather than left implied.

_xs_reversal_tuning_note:
2026-09-07, C10 wide search (108 cells, panel split into THIRDS, a cell must be positive in all three). The previous live cell - momentum 3d / 24h hold / top 10% - was NOT one of them: its thirds run +0.56 / -0.88 / +2.93. A negative third on the config that is actually trading real money.
Moved to 3d / 72h / top 2%, thirds +2.22 / +1.91 / +2.86 - positive in all three and the most consistent cell in the search by worst-third.
Dollars, at $33.66 notional and 3 slots, are the reason and not the EV per trade:
  cell                  mean    worst third   trades/day   $/mo mean   $/mo worst
  3d/24h/top10% (old)  +0.87%     -0.88%          3.0        +26.36      -26.66
  3d/72h/top2%  (new)  +2.33%     +1.91%          1.0        +23.53      +19.29
Nearly identical at the mean; the old cell LOSES $27/mo in a period like its own middle third, the new one makes $19. Same signal, same code path - only hold_hours and top_pct move.
WIRING: the book overrides the DSL per position via bounded_exit_override, setting hard_timeout_minutes = hold_hours*60 (4320) and stale_flat_timeout_minutes = 0 (disabled, dsl_exit.py:258 gates on > 0). The GLOBAL dsl_exit hard_timeout of 30h and stale_flat of 8h therefore do NOT truncate the 72h hold. Checked, because both are shorter than the hold and would have cut it short if the override did not exist.
COST: turnover falls 3.0 -> 1.0 trades/day, so the forward ledger now needs ~37 days to reach the ~37 resolved bets that pin the true EV to +/-1%, against ~12 before. That is the real price of this change and it is worth paying: the old cell's evidence would have accumulated faster around a config with a losing third.
STILL A BACKTEST. 33 of 108 cells pass the all-thirds filter and picking among them is selection. What is NOT selection is the comparison that drove this: the live cell failed a stability criterion declared before looking, and a same-signal alternative passed it.

copycat._note:
2026-10-02, operator build. UNTESTED: no backtest for the 10-wallet rule itself (unlike copy_trade's W-CP1, which backtested and REFUTED copying 0xe282 -- one of these 10 leaders -- at every 2025-03..10 start month, 0.5x-3x). enabled false until the operator reviews the dashboard panel and flips it on: this is real money mirrored across up to 10 wallets at once, not one.

REAL EQUITY IS $1.29. That is the whole reason fixed_margin is the default sizing_mode instead of proportional: at $1.29, sleeve_frac x equity is sub-cent, so the proportional formula (leader's % move x our equity x sleeve_frac) rounds to a copy under the exchange's $10.50 minimum on every single trade -- min_order_bump would be bumping to the floor every time, which defeats being proportional at all. fixed_margin instead pins OUR margin per copy to a flat dollar amount, independent of equity and of the leader's size: fixed_margin_usd 0.25 at max leverage 50x is $0.25 x 50 = $12.50 of notional per copy, comfortably over the $10.50 floor.

sizing_mode:
  'fixed_margin' (DEFAULT) -- every copy posts fixed_margin_usd of margin, at whatever leverage leverage_mode selects. Notional = fixed_margin_usd x that leverage. Ignores the leader's size and our equity -- same dollar risk on every copy, which is the only sizing that makes sense at $1.29.
  'fixed_notional' -- every copy opens at a flat fixed_notional_usd of notional regardless of leverage (higher leverage puts in LESS margin for the same notional -- the inverse of fixed_margin). Floored at the $10.50 exchange minimum: the config value itself must be >= 10.50.
  'proportional' -- the ORIGINAL design: our notional = size_multiplier x (the leader's added notional / his equity) x our equity x sleeve_frac -- we take the same percentage move he took, scaled by size_multiplier. Only mode where size_multiplier, sleeve_frac and the leader's own equity matter to sizing. Correct at real account sizes; at $1.29 it mostly produces sub-floor copies that min_order_bump then bumps to $10.50 anyway, which is exactly why it is not the default right now.
size_multiplier 1.0: proportional-mode-only scalar on the leader's percentage move. Range 0..100; irrelevant under fixed_margin/fixed_notional.
fixed_margin_usd 0.25: margin per copy in fixed_margin mode -- $12.50 notional at max_position_leverage 50. Raise this once equity grows past a few dollars.
fixed_notional_usd 10.5: notional per copy in fixed_notional mode, floored at the exchange minimum -- cannot usefully be set lower.

leverage_mode:
  'max' (DEFAULT) -- open each mirrored coin at its own exchange max leverage (capped by max_position_leverage).
  'match' -- open at the LEADER's own leverage on that coin instead (still capped by max_position_leverage).
  'fixed' -- ignore the coin's max and the leader's leverage; always use the flat `leverage` setting below (still capped by max_position_leverage and by whatever the exchange allows on that coin).
leverage 20: used when leverage_mode is 'fixed'. Range 1..50; irrelevant under 'max' or 'match'.
max_position_leverage 50: hard cap applied under every leverage_mode -- the one setting that bounds worst-case leverage no matter what the other three say.

margin_mode 'isolated' walls each mirrored position's margin off from the rest of the account, so one liquidation cannot cross into another position; 'cross' shares margin account-wide -- more capital-efficient per position, but one bad coin's margin draw can drag the others into liquidation too.

leader_overrides {}: per-leader exceptions. Keys are leader addresses (lowercase, must already be in `leaders` to take effect); values are any subset of {sizing_mode, size_multiplier, fixed_margin_usd, fixed_notional_usd, leverage_mode, leverage, margin_mode, max_worse_entry_pct} -- anything not present falls through to the book-level setting above. copycat_live.leader_settings(config, leader) computes the effective (overridden) dict per leader; the dashboard panel shows that, never the raw override, so it can never disagree with what maybe_run actually uses. Empty by default: no leader is special-cased yet. A write here merges into the existing per-leader dict, never replaces the whole leader_overrides block or another leader's entry -- merge_agent_config's recursive deep-merge already guarantees this for any nested dict (proven in tests/test_copycat_wiring.py), so the write endpoint needed no extra merge logic of its own.

include_spot_staked false: size a leader's equity off his perp account value only, ignoring spot/staked balance (proportional mode only; fixed_margin/fixed_notional ignore his equity entirely). only_new_positions false: mirror a leader's FULL current book the first time we see him, not only positions he opens afterward -- true is safer (mirrors only decisions made after we started watching, same default copy_trade uses) but starts the book blind to whatever he already holds; set true once this book has live evidence of its own. max_worse_entry_pct 10.0: skip a copy once price has already moved more than 10% worse than the leader's own entry since he opened it, so a stale or delayed mirror cannot chase an entry arbitrarily far from his. min_order_bump true: round a copy's notional UP to the exchange minimum when the computed size falls short, so the position still opens (copy_trade instead skips sub-$10.50 copies outright -- this book bumps up instead; moot in fixed_notional mode, which is already floored at $10.50).

sleeve_frac 0.25: this book's share of account equity, before the per-leader split -- only load-bearing in proportional mode (fixed_margin/fixed_notional size off their own usd settings instead, not off equity at all).

THE RISK, plainly: up to 10 live wallets, isolated-or-cross, up to 50x, no stop anywhere in the rule, same as copy_trade's one leader. A leader liquidating or dumping is mirrored with zero delay-adjustment beyond max_worse_entry_pct. This is an operator decision, not evidence -- see W-CP1 and copy_trade's own override note above.
